scenario.name: Kaspersky GReAT, Citizen Lab & Amnesty MVT — iOS Operation Triangulation Zero-Click iMessage & Shutdown.log Forensics (CVE-2023-41990)
scenario.overview: Imagine a live television and radio broadcast studio with a glowing red ON AIR sign, a soundproof control-room window, a sliding mixing console, and a rooftop signal dish. Slipping into the broadcast control room beside the soundproof glass window, an unlisted engineer patches a covert jumper cord straight into the live mixing console. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the soundproof on air studio door in tiny disguised batches, then bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the mixing console & roof satellite dish. The master control broadcast log spots an unscheduled auxiliary transmitter channel pulling signal off the mixing board and cuts the rogue patch. In this scenario (T1456, Kaspersky GReAT, Citizen Lab & Amnesty MVT, iOS Operation Triangulation Zero-Click iMessage & Shutdown.log Forensics , CVE-2023-41990), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: hidden iMessage Attachment Processing, then ephemeral Implant Execution, then anomalous System Process Cellular/Wi-Fi. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Hidden iMessage Attachment Processing, then Ephemeral Implant Execution, then Anomalous System Process Cellular/Wi-Fi, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1456 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Hidden iMessage Attachment Processing in IMTranscoderAgent & Font Parser Crash Trace
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1456 - Drive-By Compromise / Zero-Click Messaging)
stages.description: Slipping into the broadcast control room beside the soundproof glass window, an unlisted engineer patches a covert jumper cord straight into the live mixing console. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the soundproof on air studio door in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the broadcast director go about their routine. When a zero-click iMessage containing a crafted font/image attachment arrives via Apple Push Notification service (apsd), imagent and IMTranscoderAgent process the attachment automatically. Forensic artifacts in CrashReporter and diagnostic logs record abnormal memory faults inside FontParser / CoreGraphics (logged in Linux Audit Event 41990 with TargetDaemon=IMTranscoderAgent , iMessage Attachment Transcoder, LibraryModule=libFontParser.dylib , TrueType ADJUST Instruction, VulnerabilityRef=CVE-2023-41990 / CVE-2023-32434 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes mvt-ios check-backup --output ./mvt-results ./ios-encrypted-backup/ (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , mvt-ios chec so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1456 during "Hidden iMessage Attachment Processing in IMTranscoderAgent & Font Parser Crash Trace"). Next, the follow-up artifact mvt-ios check-iocs --iocs triangulation.stix2 ./mvt-results/ runs (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , mvt-ios chec so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1456 during "Hidden iMessage Attachment Processing in IMTranscoderAgent & Font Parser Crash Trace"). stages.title: Stage 2: Ephemeral Implant Execution in /private/var/tmp/ Recorded in iOS Shutdown.log
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1070.004 - Indicator Removal: File Deletion / Shutdown.log)
stages.description: As the red ON AIR sign lights up above the studio floor, the covert bridge silently mirrors every studio feed up to the spinning rooftop signal dish. Here in Step 2 inside the broadcast studio, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the mixing console & roof satellite dish without disturbing the backup emergency transmitter. Even though the in-memory implant removes its temporary files from /private/var/tmp/ after execution and does not survive a reboot, the iOS kernel writes every unclosed process PID and path active during system shutdown into /private/var/db/diagnostics/Shutdown.log (extracted from a sysdiagnose archive) (logged in Linux Audit Event 38606 with ForensicArtifactFile=/private/var/db/diagnostics/Shutdown.log , sysdiagnose, RecordedProcessPath=/private/var/tmp/main, ForensicSignificance=Proves execution of deleted binary from world-writable /private/var/tmp/ so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes grep -E "/private/var/tmp/|/private/var/db/" sysdiagnose_extracted/logs/Shutdown/shutdown.log (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , grep -E "/pr so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1070.004 during "Ephemeral Implant Execution in /private/var/tmp/ Recorded in iOS Shutdown.log"). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ /private/var/tmp/main (Recorded in /private/var/db/diagnostics/Shutdown.log) / ⇠#2 ACK 38606) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 IMTranscoderAgent / BlastDoor), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Shutdown.log & DataUsage.sqlite).

keySpecs.value: Collect a full iOS sysdiagnose archive prior to wiping a suspected device and run mvt-ios over Shutdown.log to identify processes that executed from /private/var/tmp/.

stages.title: Stage 3: Anomalous System Process Cellular/Wi-Fi Exfiltration in DataUsage.sqlite & netusage.sqlite
stages.subtitle: Exfiltration (T1041 - Exfiltration Over C2 Channel)
stages.description: Outside the building, the intruder tunes in to every private studio channel in real time while the broadcast director hears zero static in the headphones. In this final step inside the broadcast studio, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the mixing console & roof satellite dish until the master control broadcast log catches the mismatch. iOS persistently tracks per-process network byte counters in /private/var/wireless/Library/Databases/DataUsage.sqlite and netusage.sqlite. MVT correlates ZPROCESS entries showing non-networked system daemons (or deleted PIDs) transmitting megabytes of HTTPS data over Wi-Fi/Cellular (logged in Network Event 443 with SqliteDatabase=DataUsage.sqlite / netusage.sqlite, AnomalousProcessName=BackupAgent , ZPROCNAME with NULL Bundle ID, OutboundBytesRecorded=14.8 MB Wi-Fi / 3.1 MB Cellular so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite "SELECT ZPROCESS.ZPROCNAME, ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME, ZLIVEUSAGE.ZWIFIIN, ZLIVEUSAGE.ZWIFIOUT FROM ZLIVEUSAGE JOIN ZPROCESS ON ZLIVEUSAGE.ZHASPROCESS = ZPROCESS.Z_PK;" (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite "SELECT ZPROCESS.ZPROCNAME, ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME, ZLI so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1041 during "Anomalous System Process Cellular/Wi-Fi Exfiltration in DataUsage.sqlite & netusage.sqlite" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite SELECT ZPROCNAME, ZWIFIOUT FROM ZLIVEUSAGE / ⇠#3 RESP 443) from Node ③ (#3 IMTranscoderAgent / BlastDoor) to Node ④ (#4 XNU Kernel & MMIO Registers), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Shutdown.log & DataUsage.sqlite).
